naming: The loader deserializes with YamlDotNet's CamelCaseNamingConvention and refuses any key it does not know.

keys.description: Optional grouping label (the source system) the platform files the flow's pipeline and runs under. A blank value counts as none.
Optional text describing what the downloads are for.
The downloads, at least one and at most 100, names unique ignoring case. Each writes every record one kind holds in the partition to a folder of its name under `target.location`.
One download: the kind it reads (`kind`), narrowed by a search `query`, written to the folder of its `name`.
Optional text describing what the download holds.
The kind read, `authority:source:entityType:version`, each segment a value, `*`, or a value with `*` inside it (`1.*.*`), matched ignoring case as the search service matches a kind.

The download's name: a letter or digit followed by letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', at most 100 characters, not ending in '.' and no Windows device name (CON, NUL, COM1, LPT1 and the like). It is the folder the download's files go to, and a run's payload (`downloads`) and the Downloads tab name it by it.
A Lucene query narrowing the records a search read lists; `{name}` tokens of `parameters` and `{partition}` are filled in. A storage read takes none, and the flow is refused when one is written.

The document kind: `download`, every record OSDU kinds hold in a partition written to a folder, a JSON file each named after its id, holding the record as storage holds it: its metadata, never a file a dataset links to. Its ledger keeps the version each file holds, so a run writes only what is new or changed and a newer version replaces the file; an id OSDU no longer serves is marked gone and its file left in place. Nothing is written to OSDU.
The download flow's name: its pipeline identity, and the name its downloads are kept under. A flow that reads partitions keeps its downloads per partition.
What one run works on at once: `recordsAtOnce`, how many storage reads a run has in flight at once. A download flow fans nothing out across the fleet.
Renamed: it is written as `parallelism.recordsAtOnce`, as on a delivery flow. A document that still declares it is refused when it loads, naming the key it is now.
How many storage reads a run has in flight at once, each of up to a hundred records (POST /query/records). At least 1.
Optional: the flow's parameters, by name. `{name}` tokens are usable in a download's `query` and in `target.location`; `{partition}` is always the partition the run reads, and may not be declared.
One parameter; `<name>` is the name its `{name}` tokens use. A run supplying a value for a name the flow does not declare is refused.

The values the parameter may take, in the order a run form lists them: a run given any other value is refused (`parameter 'name' is given 'x', which is not one of its choices: a, b.`), and the run form offers them as a list to pick from. At least one and at most 500, each listed once and written as a run gives it; a `default` is one of them. Leave it out for a parameter that takes any value.
One value the parameter may take.
The value used when a run supplies none; one of the parameter's `choices` when it lists them.
Text describing what the parameter is for.
When true, a run that supplies no value, for a parameter without a default, fails with "parameter 'name' is required". A scheduled fire supplies only the schedule's `values`, so give it one there.

The OSDU data partitions the flow downloads from, hard-coded: each by its `data-partition-id` written literally, never a reference, at least one, unique ignoring case. Leave it out to read the partition `source.headers` names, or every partition registered with the catalog when the headers name none. A run reads one partition.
One partition the flow downloads from, by its `data-partition-id`.
The HTTP settings: timeout, retry, rate limit, TLS, URL allowlist and response size. What runs at once is `parallelism`.
Not a setting here any more: a delivery flow writes it as `parallelism.recordsPerBatch`, and a download flow has no use for it. A document that still declares it is refused when it loads; remove it.
Not a setting any more: a worker claims the records due for a retry `parallelism.recordsAtOnce` at a time, at least 50. A document that still declares it is refused when it loads; remove it.

Not a setting here any more: it is written as `parallelism.recordsAtOnce`, since what runs at once, and across the fleet, is the flow's parallelism, and reliability keeps what makes a request hold. A document that still declares it here is refused when it loads, naming where it goes.
Not a setting here any more: a delivery flow writes it as `parallelism.nodes`, and a download flow has no use for it. A document that still declares it is refused when it loads; remove it.
Not a setting here any more: a delivery flow writes it as `parallelism.minRowsPerNode`, and a download flow has no use for it. A document that still declares it is refused when it loads; remove it.
A delivery flow's setting: how long a worker's lease on a record lasts. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a download flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: the target's declared request body ceiling (0 = not declared). The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a download flow does not use it.
The largest response body read, in bytes. A larger response fails the request with a message naming this setting.
Not a setting here any more: a delivery flow writes it as `parallelism.interfacesAtOnce`, and a download flow has no use for it. A document that still declares it is refused when it loads; remove it.
The most requests per second the flow sends to the platform; 0 means unlimited. Token requests are not limited.
Not a setting here any more: a delivery flow writes it as `parallelism.renderThreads`, and a download flow has no use for it. A document that still declares it is refused when it loads; remove it.
How one request is repeated inline. Only requests that are safe to repeat are repeated, on 408, 425, 429, 503 and 504 and on a transport failure; 500 and 502 are not replayed.
The most attempts one request gets, the first included.
The wait between attempts: `exponential` doubles `baseDelayMs` per attempt, `fixed` waits `baseDelayMs` each time; both are capped at `maxDelayMs`.
The first wait between attempts, in milliseconds.

Whether a `Retry-After` the service sends is honoured. A requested wait within `maxDelayMs` becomes the floor of the backoff; a longer one is never shortened, so the request stops instead of waiting it out.
The longest wait between attempts, in milliseconds.
A delivery flow's setting: the first wait between a record's attempts across worker passes, in minutes. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a download flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: the longest wait between a record's attempts across worker passes, in minutes. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a download flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: statuses that hold a record instead of retrying it. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a download flow does not use it.
One HTTP status code.
How long one HTTP request may take, in seconds.

The hosts requests may reach (an SSRF guard), checked on every request and every redirect hop. Empty allows any host the deployment's network policy reaches; token requests are not checked against it.
A host name, or `*.suffix` to match the bare domain and any subdomain of it. Compared ignoring case.
Whether the platform's TLS certificate is verified. `false` also needs `SQLFLOW_DELIVERY_ALLOW_INSECURE_TLS=true` on the node, or the run is refused.
The OSDU platform the downloads are read from, and how. A run only reads: nothing is ever written to OSDU.

How requests to the OSDU platform authenticate, written as `target.auth` is on a delivery flow. Secrets are references only: ${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}. Left out, requests carry no credentials (type `none`).
keys.appliesWhen: Optional; written as `target.auth` on a delivery flow.

keys.description: The header an `apiKeyHeader` auth sends the key in.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is apiKeyHeader, which needs it.

keys.description: The secondary secret, as a reference (${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}): the username for `basic`, the client id for `oauth2ClientCredentials` (sent as `client_id` unless the token body names one).

The primary secret, as a reference (${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}), never a literal: the token for `bearer`, the key for `apiKeyHeader`, the password for `basic`, the client secret for `oauth2ClientCredentials` (sent as `client_secret` unless the token body names one). A literal is refused when the flow is read.
keys.appliesWhen: Needed by bearer, apiKeyHeader and basic; used by oauth2ClientCredentials.

keys.description: The OAuth2 token endpoint: where a token is requested and how it is read from the answer. One token serves the run and is requested again shortly before it expires.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is oauth2ClientCredentials, which needs it.

keys.description: The text put before the access token in the `Authorization` header.
When true, the client id and secret are sent as an HTTP Basic `Authorization` header on the token request instead of in its form body.

Extra form fields of the token request, by name. `grant_type` is `client_credentials` unless set here, and `client_id` and `client_secret` come from `secondarySecretRef` and `secretRef` unless set here. A field named as a secret (`client_secret`, `password`, `refresh_token`, `client_assertion`, ...) holds a reference only; a literal there is refused when the flow is read. `client_id`, `scope` and `audience` may be literals.

One form field of the token request; `<name>` is the field name (such as `scope`). The value may be a reference (${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}), resolved before the request is sent. A field named as a secret must be a reference.

An OIDC discovery document whose `token_endpoint` is the token URL. When set it is used instead of `url`; it may be a reference. Written literally, its user info and query may carry no credential: one that does is refused when the flow is read.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is oauth2ClientCredentials; give this or url.

keys.description: The path of the access token in the token endpoint's JSON answer.
The token endpoint URL, usually a reference such as `${env:OSDU_TOKEN_URL}`. Written literally, its user info and query may carry no credential: one that does is refused when the flow is read.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is oauth2ClientCredentials; give this or discoveryUrl.

keys.description: The auth scheme: `none`, `bearer` (a token as a reference), `apiKeyHeader` (a key in a named header), `basic` (username and password) or `oauth2ClientCredentials` (a token requested from `token`). Read ignoring case.
The text put before the secret in the header value of a `bearer` or `apiKeyHeader` auth. An OAuth2 token takes `token.applyPrefix` instead.
The base URL of the OSDU platform, usually a reference such as `${env:OSDU_URL}`. Written literally, its user info and query may carry no credential: one that does is refused when the flow is read.
Headers sent with every request. A flow that names its partitions, or reads every registered one, may not name `data-partition-id` here: each run sets it to the partition it reads.

One header; `<name>` is the header name (`data-partition-id: dev`). A value may be a reference (${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}). A header that carries a credential (`Authorization`, an API or subscription key, a token, any `x-api-*` header) holds a reference, after its scheme when it has one (`Bearer ${env:NAME}`); a literal is refused when the flow is read.

Storage's read of up to 1,000 records' system properties by id (openapi storage v2, POST /query/records/headers). Where a deployment does not serve it (404 or 405), records are read through `recordQueryPath`, a hundred at a time.

How a read of every record a search matches pages through them. `cursor` (the default) pages the search service's cursor (POST /query_with_cursor), a context the service holds between pages and moves on with each, so a read that loses a page reads the search again from its first page. `createTime` pages the plain search (POST /query) in the order of each record's createTime and then its id, each page asked from the last record handed out: the service holds nothing between pages, a page that fails is asked again from where the read stopped, and a read that comes back short reads again only the batch of about 10,000 records it is short in. Either way a search is read whole or the read fails.
The search service's offset search, which a plan counts a download's records through (openapi search v2, POST /query).

How the downloads list OSDU. `search` (the default) pages the search index with a viewer's entitlements; the index lags writes and leaves out a record it failed to index, so a record written seconds before, or never indexed, is not listed, and no file is written for it until it is. `storage` lists every active record of each kind from storage itself (GET /query/records?kind=, which needs the storage service's admin role) and reads their system properties a thousand at a time: the complete answer, unindexed records included. A kind with wildcards is expanded through the schema service for a storage read. Either way, every record written is read from storage (POST /query/records), a hundred at a time.

Storage's listing of a kind's record ids (GET) for a storage read, and its read of records by id (POST), a hundred at a time, which every record written is read through; openapi storage v2 /query/records.
The schema service, which expands a kind with wildcards into the kinds a storage read lists one at a time.
The search service's cursor search, which a search read pages a download through, a thousand ids a page, whole or failing (openapi search v2, POST /query_with_cursor).
Where the files go: each download writes into a folder of its name under `location`, a file per record named after its id (`:` written `~`, `%` written `=`).

The folder each download's folder is made in: an absolute local path, or an `abfss://` or `https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net` URI, with `{partition}` and `{parameter}` tokens; `{run}` and `{date}` are refused, since every run writes to the same folder. A relative path is refused (a run reads its flow from a checkout of its own), and so is a `${...}` reference or a credential in the URI: Azure Storage is written with the node's own Azure credential. A run that writes to another folder than the last one did writes every record again.

What the correlation id every OSDU request of the flow's runs carries names: `correlation-id: osdu-delivery-<repository>-<operation>-<run id>`, the repository's code from the `osdu-delivery.yaml` nearest above the flow. Left out, the runs name the kind's own operation code.
The flow's operation code in its runs' correlation id: a lower-case letter, then lower-case letters and digits, at most 16 in all and no hyphen. Defaults to the kind's own, `dwn`.
